acceptedAnswer.text: Contrast describes differences between tones, colours, textures or ideas in a photograph. These differences can separate elements, suggest relationships and influence where the viewer’s attention goes.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between high and low contrast?

acceptedAnswer.text: High contrast involves stronger differences, while low contrast involves gentler differences. The best choice depends on the photograph’s meaning, detail and atmosphere.

mainEntity.name: Does high contrast require pure black and white?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Strong differences can exist without pure black shadows or pure white highlights. Clipping is a separate issue, so decide which highlight and shadow detail matters before allowing it to disappear.

mainEntity.name: Are high key and low contrast the same thing?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. High key describes an image dominated by lighter tones. Low contrast describes relatively gentle differences. A high key photograph can still contain a strongly contrasting dark element.

mainEntity.name: Does a higher white-balance Temp setting make a photograph warmer?

acceptedAnswer.text: For the same raw photograph in Lightroom Classic, raising the Temp value makes the rendering warmer and lowering it makes the rendering cooler. This compensation control differs from describing the colour temperature of the original light source.

mainEntity.name: Should I always increase contrast when editing?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The existing contrast may already express what matters. Compare the starting image with stronger and gentler treatments, then keep a change only when it supports your intention.
Conceptual contrast is a relationship between different ideas or subjects, such as old and new or activity and stillness. It depends on context and meaning rather than brightness or colour alone.

mainEntity.name: How does contrast relate to restraint?

acceptedAnswer.text: Restraint means deciding which differences deserve emphasis and which ones compete with the photograph’s purpose. It may involve reducing a bright distraction, preserving subtle colour or leaving an unnecessary edit unused.
